paper: Gerber, Bergemann et al. 2023, A&A 669, A43 (arXiv 2206.00967)
provenance_caveat: NO DOI, mutable Seafile -> md5-pinned (RYA-540). The payload was ALREADY STAGED on Sirius before this ticket: RYA-785 was filed saying atom.fe607a was 'AVAILABLE-NEVER-PULLED', but all three files were on disk. What was missing was this provenance record — the element status tracker reads the REGISTRATION, not the disk, so an unregistered-but-present deck reads as never fetched. Nothing was re-downloaded; the staged bytes were md5'd in place.

deck_abundance.why: NOT the 7.50 printed in the atom.fe607a header. bsyn STOPs with 'NLTE departure coeff calculated for abundance = 7.46 while it is 7.50 here' — the departure coefficients were computed at 7.46, so the synthesis must run at 7.46 or they do not apply. A property of the deck, not a fitted value.

gate.ticket: RYA-534 element-general gate; adjudicated in the RYA-785 second pass
gate.lines: Fe I 5461.549 / 5607.664 / 5905.671 / 6597.559 / 6705.117 / 6726.666 / 6828.591 / 6837.005 -- eight lines, selected by scripts/rya785_pick_gate_lines.py against FIVE requirements: both GES NLTE levels identified (the Co/Ni silent-departure=1 trap), present in the committed MPIA per-line grid (so a cross-engine diagnostic exists), measured in-aggregate by us, not weak (the Ti trap), and ISOLATED -- no other Fe I inside the gate's own 1.2 A EW integration window at > loggf-1.5. Only 9 of 57 candidates survive isolation.
gate.anchor: +0.06 -- Gerber, Bergemann et al. 2023, A&A 669 A43, THE DECK'S OWN PAPER. Table 3 gives the solar [Fe/H] as -0.04 (1D LTE) -> +0.02 (1D NLTE); Table 4 states the correction as +0.06 dex; Sect. 5.1 reports 'an average difference of about +0.05 dex between the [Fe/H] determined using 1D NLTE and 1D LTE' across their sample.
gate.result: per-line +0.0500 / +0.0636 / +0.0524 / +0.0747 / +0.0686 / +0.0501 / +0.0579 (n=7 used); median +0.0579, mean +0.0596, sd 0.0097. Fe I 5607.664 EXCLUDED by the SYN_EW_MIN=5 mA guard (synthetic EW 0.95 mA). Including it the median is +0.0589, so the exclusion is not what decides the verdict. Reproduced bit-for-bit across two runs.
gate.verdict: PASS -- |median - anchor| = 0.0021 <= tol 0.05. The deck reproduces its own published solar Fe NLTE correction to ~0.002 dex on eight independent isolated lines, and every line returns a positive delta in a tight +0.050..+0.075 band.
gate.first_pass_was_CHECK_and_why: The first pass returned CHECK at |median - anchor| = 0.051 vs tol 0.05 -- a miss by 0.001 dex -- because it anchored on the median of the gate lines' own Bergemann-MPIA deltas (+0.0124). THAT IS THE WRONG REFEREE. MPIA is a different model atom; RYA-785 requires validation against the deck's own published anchor and forbids MPIA as the target, and RYA-525/712 classify a Gerber-vs-MPIA difference as a cross-engine DIAGNOSTIC, never a validation criterion -- a deck cannot fail for disagreeing with a different deck. The first pass also had a contaminated line set: of its three lines only 5905.671 was isolated (5806.725 has an Fe I neighbour at 0.098 A, 6027.070 at 0.239 A, both inside the 1.2 A EW window, where a SAME-SPECIES blend does not cancel in the EW->A* inversion the way a different-species blend does). The one clean line returned +0.0636, against the published +0.06. THE TOLERANCE WAS NOT CHANGED (0.05 in both passes) -- only the anchor and the line set, both on stated evidence.
gate.cross_engine_diagnostic: RYA-525, never folded into the error bar: these eight lines' own Bergemann-MPIA deltas have median +0.0118, so the Gerber deck runs ~5x MPIA on the same transitions. That is the THIRD instance of the Gerber-vs-MPIA model-atom systematic already on record -- Ti (~2x) and Mn (~1/2, where the Mn prov note records TS-Gerber +0.043 vs Bergemann +0.107). It is a FINDING about the two model atoms, not a defect in either.
harness_defects_found: First pass: the gate reported a plausible +0.300 from a TWO-DAY-OLD Fe_nlte.spec, because `os.path.exists()` cannot tell 'this run wrote it' from 'a previous run left it' in the shared, never-cleaned {W}/work directory. Fixed by an mtime stale guard on the interpolator, babsma and bsyn outputs.

Second pass: the Ti 'weak lines' rule was being enforced on the MEASURED EW, but the COG inversion consumes the SYNTHETIC EW, and the two can disagree by 21x (Fe I 5607.664: measured 20.1 mA, synthesised 0.95 mA). Added SYN_EW_MIN = 5 mA, applied to the quantity that actually matters. 5607.664 is registered in problem_children.csv as the RYA-713 ATOMIC-DATA pattern.
Second pass: line selection had no ISOLATION requirement, so it could pick a blended pair and report it as one line. Now requirement (5).
gate.wiring_status: VALIDATED BUT NOT WIRED. derive_band_products.py --engine-b-deck gerber-nlte still refuses, and the refusal message was corrected: the old text said 'not provisioned', which is now false. The real blocker is plumbing -- iSpec's TS wrapper does accept `nlte_departure_coefficients`, but `_fit_synth_flux` has no NLTE parameter and iSpec's own dep-grid store (input/dep-grid/) is EMPTY, while our deck is TS-native (atom.* + auxData + .bin), consumed today only by this gate's direct interpol_modeles_nlte + bsyn calls. ⚠️ iSpec also fails SOFT: an element whose linelist rows carry no NLTE label lands in `nlte_ignored` and synthesis proceeds in LTE without raising (the RYA-764 trap), so the wiring owes a hard check on `nlte_available`.
